q: What type of reaction is CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂?
why: Two substances combine to form a single product.

q: Iron nails are left in blue copper sulphate solution and the colour slowly fades. Why?
c: Iron displaces copper from copper sulphate
Copper displaces iron from iron sulphate
The water evaporates and takes the colour with it
why: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it takes copper's place: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu.

q: In the reaction 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, magnesium is
why: Magnesium gains oxygen (and loses electrons), so it is oxidised.

q: Green ferrous sulphate crystals are heated. They turn white, then brown, and a smell of burning sulphur is given off. What type of reaction is this?
why: One substance breaks down into several: 2FeSO₄ → Fe₂O₃ + SO₂ + SO₃.

q: Respiration releases energy. What kind of reaction is it?
why: A reaction that gives out energy is exothermic.

q: Sodium sulphate solution is mixed with barium chloride solution and a white solid appears. The white solid is
why: A double displacement: BaSO₄ is insoluble and precipitates; NaCl stays dissolved.

q: Which of these solutions is the most acidic?
why: The lower the pH below 7, the more acidic the solution.

q: A solution turns red litmus blue. Its pH is most likely
why: Turning red litmus blue shows a base, and bases have pH above 7.

q: Which gas is given off when zinc granules react with dilute sulphuric acid?
why: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂; the gas burns with a pop.

q: The chemical formula of Plaster of Paris is
why: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate; with water it sets back into gypsum, CaSO₄·2H₂O.

q: Tooth decay starts when the pH in the mouth falls below about
why: Below about pH 5.5, acids from bacteria start to dissolve tooth enamel.

q: Baking soda in a cake mix makes the cake rise when it is baked. What does that?
c: Hydrogen released from the hydrogen carbonate
Carbon dioxide released when it is heated or reacts with an acid
why: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂; the gas puffs up the cake.

q: Washing soda is
why: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate; NaHCO₃ is baking soda and CaOCl₂ is bleaching powder.

q: Which of these metals will give hydrogen gas with dilute hydrochloric acid?
why: Only metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series displace it; zinc is, the others are not.

q: An ionic compound such as sodium chloride conducts electricity
c: When molten or dissolved in water
why: Its ions can only move, and carry charge, once it is melted or dissolved.

q: When sodium chloride forms, each sodium atom
why: Na → Na⁺ + e⁻; chlorine gains that electron. Ionic bonds come from transfer, not sharing.

q: Galvanising protects iron by coating it with
why: A layer of zinc keeps air and water off the iron, and corrodes first if scratched.

q: Metal X is found as the free metal in nature and does not react with oxygen even when heated. X is most likely
why: Only the least reactive metals, at the bottom of the reactivity series, are found uncombined.

q: Which conditions are needed for iron to rust?
why: Rusting needs oxygen and water together.

q: The bond between the two carbon atoms in ethane (C₂H₆) is
why: Ethane is saturated: every carbon–carbon bond is single.

q: Which of these is an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
why: Ethene has a carbon–carbon double bond; the others are alkanes with single bonds only.

q: CH₄ and C₂H₆ are the first two members of a homologous series. The next member is
why: Each member adds CH₂: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ with n = 3 gives C₃H₈.

q: Why do most carbon compounds not conduct electricity?
c: Their bonds are covalent, so they have no ions or free electrons
why: Covalent compounds don't form ions, so nothing carries the charge.

q: Ethanol reacts with sodium metal to give
why: 2Na + 2CH₃CH₂OH → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂.

q: Soap forms a scum instead of lather in hard water because
c: It reacts with calcium and magnesium salts to form an insoluble substance
why: Calcium and magnesium ions precipitate the soap; detergents avoid this.

q: During photosynthesis a plant takes in
why: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ with light and chlorophyll.

q: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces
why: Yeast ferments glucose to ethanol and CO₂; lactic acid is made in muscles.

q: The basic filtering unit of the kidney is the
why: Each kidney has about a million nephrons that filter the blood.

q: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs?
why: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; the pulmonary artery is the one artery carrying deoxygenated blood.

q: Water rises up the xylem of a tall tree mainly because of
c: Transpiration pull as water evaporates from the leaves
why: Evaporation from the leaves draws a continuous column of water up the xylem.

q: Bile helps digestion by
c: Killing every bacterium in the gut
Breaking fats into small droplets (emulsifying them)
why: Bile has no enzymes; it emulsifies fats so lipase can work on them.

q: You pull your hand away from a hot plate before you feel pain. The response is coordinated by
why: This is a reflex arc through the spinal cord; the brain is told afterwards.

q: Which plant hormone makes a shoot bend towards light by making cells grow longer on the shaded side?
why: Auxin collects on the shaded side and speeds up cell elongation there.

q: Iodised salt is recommended because iodine is needed to make
why: The thyroid gland uses iodine to make thyroxin; too little causes goitre.

q: Insulin is secreted by the
why: Insulin from the pancreas lowers blood sugar.

q: The gap between two neurons is called a
why: Chemicals carry the signal across the synapse to the next neuron.

q: A shoot growing towards light and a root growing towards water are examples of
why: Growth towards light is phototropism; towards water is hydrotropism.

q: Amoeba reproduces by
why: Amoeba splits into two daughter cells.

q: Yeast and Hydra reproduce asexually by
why: A small outgrowth (bud) develops and separates.

q: Gametes have half the number of chromosomes of body cells because they are made by
why: Meiosis halves the chromosome number, so fertilisation restores it.

q: The transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma is called
why: Fertilisation comes later, when a male gamete fuses with the egg in the ovule.

q: Sugarcane and roses are grown from pieces of stem. This is
why: New plants grow from vegetative parts (stem, root or leaf), without seeds.

q: The sex of a human child is decided by
c: The chromosome in the father's sperm
why: Eggs always carry X; sperm carry X or Y.

q: Mendel crossed pure tall (TT) and pure dwarf (tt) pea plants, then self-pollinated the F1. What fraction of the F2 plants were dwarf?
why: F1 are all Tt; Tt × Tt gives TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1, so 1/4 are dwarf (tt).

q: All of Mendel's F1 plants from the tall × dwarf cross were tall because
c: Tall plants are more common in nature
why: The dwarf allele is still there in the F1 (it reappears in F2); it is recessive.

q: A pea plant with genotype Tt is crossed with one that is tt. The expected ratio of tall to dwarf offspring is
why: Tt × tt gives Tt and tt in equal numbers.

q: A variation can be passed to the next generation only if it is in
c: The DNA of the germ cells
Changes the parent's body made during its life
why: Changes acquired during a lifetime are not in the germ-cell DNA, so they are not inherited.

q: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Where is the image formed?
c: 15 cm in front of the mirror
30 cm in front of the mirror
why: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f with u = −30 and f = −15 gives v = −30 cm: at the centre of curvature.

q: The refractive index of water is 1.33 and the speed of light in air is 3 × 10⁸ m/s. The speed of light in water is about
why: v = c/n = (3 × 10⁸)/1.33 ≈ 2.25 × 10⁸ m/s; light is slower in water.

q: The power of a convex lens of focal length 50 cm is
why: P = 1/f in metres = 1/0.5 = +2 D; a convex lens has positive power.

q: Which mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
why: A convex mirror gives an upright image and a wider field of view.

q: A ray of light passing from air into glass at an angle bends
why: It slows down in glass, so it bends towards the normal.

q: A convex lens forms a real, inverted image the same size as the object. Where is the object?
c: At 2F, twice the focal length from the lens
why: Only an object at 2F gives a same-size real image, also at 2F.

q: Myopia (short-sightedness) is corrected with
why: A concave lens diverges the rays so the image moves back onto the retina.

q: The clear sky looks blue because
c: The sun gives out only blue light
Air molecules scatter blue light more than red light
why: Shorter wavelengths are scattered more by the tiny particles of air.

q: The splitting of white light into its colours by a prism is called
why: Each colour refracts by a slightly different amount, spreading into a spectrum.

q: The eye's ability to change the focal length of its lens is called
why: Ciliary muscles change the lens's shape to focus near or far.

q: Stars twinkle because
c: Their light is refracted by layers of the atmosphere that keep changing
why: Atmospheric refraction makes the apparent brightness and position flicker.

q: A person can read a distant sign clearly but needs to hold a book far away to read it. This person has
why: Near objects focus behind the retina: hypermetropia, corrected with a convex lens.

q: A current of 0.5 A flows through a 10 Ω resistor. The potential difference across it is
Two 6 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. Their combined resistance is
why: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/6 = 1/3, so R = 3 Ω: adding a parallel path lowers resistance.

q: In a series circuit, the current
c: Is zero after the last resistor
Is the same at every point
Is largest just after the positive terminal
Is used up a little by each resistor
why: Charge is not used up; the same current flows all the way round.

q: A wire is replaced by one of the same material and thickness but twice as long. Its resistance
why: R = ρl/A, so doubling the length doubles R.

q: An electric heater draws 5 A from a 220 V supply. Its power is
The resistivity of a wire depends on
why: Resistivity is a property of the material; length and area change resistance, not resistivity.

q: Conventional current is shown flowing from + to −. In the wire, electrons actually flow
c: From the negative terminal to the positive terminal
From the positive terminal to the negative terminal
why: Electrons are negative, so they move opposite to conventional current.

q: The direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is given by
why: Thumb: force, first finger: field, second finger: current.

q: Inside a long current-carrying solenoid, the magnetic field lines are
why: The field inside a long solenoid is nearly uniform.

q: A fuse protects a circuit by
c: Melting and breaking the circuit when the current is too large
why: The fuse wire has a low melting point and heats up when the current is too big.

q: Domestic electricity supply in India is AC with a frequency of
why: India's mains supply is 220 V at 50 Hz.

q: The earth wire of an electric iron with a metal body
c: Is not needed for metal appliances
Carries current safely to the ground if the body becomes live
why: It gives a low-resistance path to earth, so touching a faulty iron doesn't shock you.

q: About how much of the energy at one trophic level passes to the next?
why: Most energy is used in life processes or lost as heat; only about 10% passes on.

q: Which of these is biodegradable?
why: Microorganisms can break down plant waste; the others persist.

q: The ozone layer in the upper atmosphere protects us from
why: Ozone absorbs most of the sun's harmful UV radiation.

q: The ozone layer has been thinned mainly by
why: CFCs from refrigerants and aerosols break down ozone.

q: A pesticide sprayed on crops gets into a food chain. Its concentration will be highest in
why: Non-biodegradable chemicals build up at each trophic level: biological magnification.
